title: Cartesian-section adjunction presentation interfaces
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$ and a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, with valuation ring $R$, uniformizer $\varpi$, and $A_n=R/\varpi^{n+1}$ for $n\in\mathbf N$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. The following are presentation types and predicates on the existing ordinary unbounded derived categories of strict semilinear systems, not assertions of their inhabitation.

For a scheme morphism $a:W\to s$, use the coefficient tower $n\mapsto A_n$ with its quotient maps, and let $\mathrm{Et}(W)$ be the derived category of strict etale systems for that tower [def-pur-etale-system-projection-data]. Its pro-etale counterpart and closed derived calculus are those of [def-coef-semilinear-derived-calculus]. A comparison-image presentation consists of the actual sequence-site inverse image $P$ and right derived direct image $R$, with the adjunction derived from the ordinary etale/pro-etale module adjunction [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism]. Define the internal-Hom representability presentation for $a$ to be the existing structure with: etale and pro-etale closed calculi; the pro-etale coefficient-system calculus; that comparison image and its tensor comparison; actual derived image along $a$; punctual sections; the ordinary sections comparison normalized by evaluation at $1$ and its derived comparison normalized by the full composed derived unit; exact finite evaluations; the identification of the two pro-etale normalization predicates; preservation of normalization by $P$; compatibility of $P$ with closed transposes; invertibility of the fiber internal-Hom comparison on normalized inputs and its identity after finite evaluation; invertibility of the etale/pro-etale internal-Hom and mapping-tower comparisons on normalized levelwise bounded constructible finite-Tor inputs; and the representing Hom bijection's evaluation formula and naturality in the arbitrary punctual test object. Internal Homs and their evaluation use [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. All these fields belong to the presentation type; no comparison functor, map or equivalence is chosen anew.

In the geometric setting and with a realization $r$, geometry $g$, sections pushforward $s$, and symmetries $\beta_X,\beta_Y$ of [def-coef-finite-adjunction-system-data], define the mapping source and target to be the actual bifunctors $(M,N)\mapsto\mathcal H_Y(r.FM,N)$ and $(M,N)\mapsto\mathcal H_X(M,r.GN)$. Their finite counterparts use exactly the recorded $F_n,G_n$ and finite global internal Homs [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus]. The enriched presentation is the existing structure comprising invertibility of the canonical internal transpose, a natural isomorphism between these mapping bifunctors whose components are derived sections of the inverse transpose, natural finite mapping isomorphisms, identification of their degree-zero maps with the specified finite adjunction, and the commuting finite-evaluation squares. The canonical transpose and global map are the ones of the realization; no arbitrary natural isomorphism replaces them.

For any ringed site with a strict coefficient tower and derived calculus $A$ as in [def-coef-semilinear-derived-calculus], define tensor-transpose coherence to be the conjunction of: evaluation of the closed transpose equals the finite closed transpose after tensor and internal-Hom evaluation, with normalized first internal-Hom input; both inverse-transpose identities; naturality of every scalar-reduction adjunct for actual system morphisms; naturality of the specified K-flat tensor-model isomorphism under morphisms of flat K-flat representatives [def-pc-kflat-complex]; and naturality of the closed transpose in both inputs. These are equations of the actual ordinary derived-system maps. The interface publicly re-exports precisely these existing definitions, with a transparent abbreviation for the internal-Hom representability presentation.
